_about: The MCP Events client table: the one source of truth for which clients are exceptions to SEP-3415's capability negotiation, and which wire dialect each needs. Wakeshift's core embeds a byte-for-byte copy (internal/mcpevents/event/mcp-events-clients.json); the TypeScript and Python SDKs ship it as generated constants without its documentation (_about, reason, source, about) or webhook_only (sdk/typescript/src/clients.ts, sdk/python/src/wakeshift/_clients.py); the Go SDK compiles in the core's copy. `go run ./internal/mcpevents/clientsgen/gen` regenerates all three, and a test in the core and in each SDK fails when a copy drifts. Test cases live in mcp-events-interop.json native_client. INPUTS: the clientInfo name (the request's _meta io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo, else the session's initialize), the HTTP User-Agent, the request's _meta, the session's initialize extensions (none on a stateless server), and whether the server serves push (events/stream). MATCH SEMANTICS: an entry matches when every field in its match holds (fields are ANDed); a field holds when any of its values does (values are ORed). NORMALIZING is ASCII only, the same in every language: a name is trimmed of spaces and tabs and its ASCII letters lowercased, anything else left as it is (Turkish İ never matches i, and NEL or a BOM neither trims nor separates tokens). client: the clientInfo name, so normalized, equals a value. client_prefix: that name starts with a value. ua_product: a User-Agent product equals a value, where the products are each token's text before its first '/', ASCII-lowercased, the tokens split on spaces and tabs only (so 'ai-sdk/2.0.97 node.js/26' has the products 'ai-sdk' and 'node.js'). meta_key: the request's _meta has a non-empty string at that key. detector: a built-in check named here and written in each codebase (chatgpt_desktop: ChatGPT's desktop app, in Codex mode or a regular chat). Values are lowercase. An entry with without_push applies only while the server doesn't serve push. The first matching entry, in file order, wins; the core's lint test fails when two entries could match the same input ambiguously. EFFECT: native never (never treated as native, whatever it declares), undeclared (native whether or not it declares the extension), or capabilities (native when it declares io.modelcontextprotocol/events in the request's _meta clientCapabilities.extensions or its session's initialize extensions). No entry matched: capabilities decide, with the spec dialect. dialect names one of dialects. webhook_only (read by the core only, so the SDKs' copies leave it out as they leave out the documentation): the client takes events by webhook alone, never poll or push, so Wakeshift's hint for an unreachable callback never suggests them (internal/appapi/callbackhint.go). An app's isNativeClient answers before any of this, for its own agents. Each entry exists only while a client deviates from the spec: the list should shrink. Nothing here is public SDK API.

spec.about: SEP-3415 as accepted: a webhook-id of its own per message, kept for its retries; gap and terminated envelopes; the spec's error codes.

draft.about: webhook-id equals the body's eventId (OpenAI's webhook profile); gap and terminated envelopes. The name is historical: every webhook made before dialects were per client was draft, and keeps it.

openclaw.about: webhook-id equals eventId; no gap or terminated (OpenClaw answers them 400); the body always has the cursor key (a missing one is 400).

chatgpt.about: OpenAI's guide: webhook-id equals eventId, no gap or terminated, ChatGPT's own error codes.

entries.reason: ChatGPT's desktop app, in Codex mode (openai-mcp (Codex) with the openai/form and text/html+skybridge capabilities) or a regular chat (openai-mcp with _meta openai/userAgent 'Codex Desktop/...'): it can't subscribe, so it keeps subscribe_events
A ChatGPT Work chat names its conversation in _meta openai/session; it subscribes without declaring the extension (it reads top-level events)
ChatGPT's MCP client (openai-mcp, openai-mcp (Codex)) subscribes without declaring and follows OpenAI's guide
ChatGPT by User-Agent (openai-mcp/1.0.0), for a request without clientInfo

OpenClaw's mcp-events plugin reads only top-level events and never declares; it refuses a webhook-id other than eventId, any gap or terminated envelope, and a body without cursor. This is the events plugin's name, not OpenClaw's tool-calling client (openclaw-bundle-mcp, bridged): if OpenClaw's tool calls ever sent openclaw, they would turn native and get vouchers nothing redeems, so the interop tests assert the name its tool calls send
opencode subscribes only with push (events/stream), which this server doesn't serve; Wakeshift's plugin wakes it. Once the server serves push, capabilities decide
opencode by User-Agent product, as opencode by name

Hermes Agent, bridged like the harnesses below (Wakeshift's plugin wakes it), in an entry of its own because it takes events by webhook alone: an unreachable callback's hint never suggests poll or push to it
Harnesses Wakeshift wakes through its own paths (a Monitor, hooks, a connector, a plugin): treating one as native would leave it with nothing listening
Hermes Agent by User-Agent product, as Hermes by name
The bridged harnesses by User-Agent product, for a request without clientInfo
The Vercel AI SDK's default client name; its webhook receiver refuses a webhook-id other than eventId
The Vercel AI SDK by User-Agent (ai-sdk/<version>), which a renamed client still sends
TanStack AI's default client name; it declares the extension but refuses a webhook-id other than eventId
